Resolves #21307

🌿 Nobody can say any more that a Neo time field ignores the time you pick from it.

`Neo.collection.Base` answers `getCanonicalKey()`, the primitive #17717 gave `Neo.data.Store` alone. A list on a plain collection, such as the time field's picker, resolves the key its item names again: an integer-keyed collection parses the fragment, as the conversion before #17717 did, and any other keeps it. `Store` keeps its model-aware override, and no call site changes, so Helix, Gallery and `list.Buffered` on a collection recover as well.

Evidence: L3 (unit specs; the clock example in Chromium against a dev server of this branch) → L3 required (AC-1 is a pick in the browser).

## AC Evidence

| AC | Evidence |
|---|---|
| AC-1 | Outside-CI: `examples/component/clock` on this branch in Chromium. Before `10:20`, clicked "12:30 AM", after `00:30`, no page error. On `dev` the same click logs `this.store.getCanonicalKey is not a function` three times and the field stays `10:20`. |
| AC-2 | CI-covered: `test/playwright/unit/collection/CanonicalKey.spec.mjs` (string-keyed, integer-keyed with refused fragments, absent value) and `test/playwright/unit/list/CollectionStore.spec.mjs` (`getItemRecordId()` on a string- and an integer-keyed collection). All five fail with `dev`'s `src/collection/Base.mjs`; the list cases with the production error. |
| AC-3 | CI-covered: the unit suite. Locally at `84cb005d58`: 7928 passed, 2 skipped. |

### 🔬 Depth Floor

**Challenge OR documented search (per guide §7.1):**

- **Challenge**: `getCanonicalKey()` delegates key-type inference to `this.getKeyType()` (`src/collection/Base.mjs:1217-1226`), which inspects `this._items[0]` (the filtered projection) rather than `(this.allItems?._items || this._items)[0]`. When an integer-keyed `Neo.collection.Base` is filtered down to `0` visible items (`_items` empty while `allItems` retains numeric-keyed items), `getKeyType()` returns `null` and `getCanonicalKey('2')` returns `'2'` instead of `2`. Benign for DOM list item clicks (an empty projection renders no items), but worth noting for programmatic callers resolving keys against a filtered-empty collection.
